in_hebrew.name: יהדי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The name Jahdai is derived from the Hebrew root 'yh' (Yah) which represents God and 'd' (dai) meaning my righteous/just one. This name could be interpreted as 'God is my righteousness' or 'God is my justifier'.

in_english.name: Jahdai

biblical_reference.note: Jahdai is a name mentioned in the Old Testament in Judges 12:4-6, where he is described as the son of Othniel and the leader of the tribe of Judah. He is said to have defeated the people of Jabesh-Gilead and brought them under the dominion of the tribe of Judah.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Jahdai" carries a unique connection to the Rastafari movement, which emerged in Jamaica during the 1930s. The name became identified with this religious and cultural movement as an expression of its devotion to the African roots of Christianity and the pan-Africanist ideals of racial pride and self-determination. The name "Jahdai" symbolizes the belief in Rastafari that God (Jah) is present in all things, and that He is a living reality that can be experienced and celebrated daily.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Jahdai" reflects a deep commitment to the spiritual beliefs and values of Christianity, particularly those connected to the Old Testament. As a name that reminds us of God as a powerful and ruling deity, "Jahdai" emphasizes faith and trust in God's sovereignty and provision. It also highlights the belief in the Hebrew tradition that God is both transcendent and immanent, present in both the natural world and in the innermost recesses of the human heart. Ultimately, the name "Jahdai" is a reminder of the enduring power and faithfulness of God, and the importance of submitting oneself to His will.

Derived from the Hebrew 'Yahweh' (I Am That I Am) and 'Dai' (throne), it signifies 'God's throne name' or 'God rules'. In the Bible, Jahdai is mentioned as a Levite who helped King David in his fight against the Philistines.
